findings.title: Loss within the host basmala's mercy frame
findings.claim: The host basmala's mercy frame holds the emphatic human-loss verdict inside compassion: the focus's general diminishment is voiced within an invocation of mercy.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier خُسْرٍ (103:2:4:1) names loss; the ordinary host preface 103:0 supplies the distinct mercy cue in الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ. Their sequential contact makes the verdict an utterance under compassion while leaving the loss itself in place.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold the severity of the loss together with the compassionate frame in which this host surah opens.
findings.containment: This is a qualified opening frame only. The basmala does not state how the loss is resolved, soften the universal assertion, or promise a specific outcome.

epistemic.reason: Both context and focus surfaces are supplied, but the relation is an interpretive effect of the host-preface placement.

findings.title: Loss brought to a day of recompense
findings.claim: Under the explicit Fātiḥa overlay, the focus's spiritual-ruin branch reaches a concrete day of judgment and recompense, so the broad loss can also be read as an outcome exposed to accounting.
findings.mechanism: The focus word خُسْرٍ can carry departure from good and ruin. The individually supplied 1:4 cue for yawm al-dīn names judgment/recompense; it contacts that branch and adds a temporal point at which the loss is assessed.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader gains a specific accountability horizon for one branch of loss, beyond the focus's broad deficit statement.
findings.containment: This is a phase-two external overlay using 1:4 alone. It does not claim that 103:2 itself names a judgment day, select a single meaning of loss, or import the whole Fātiḥa as one frame.

epistemic.reason: The individual external ayah and focus branch are supplied, but their accountability relation is an interpretive overlay and the external context is a lean cue projection.

findings.title: Loss as departure from the guided path
findings.claim: Under the explicit Fātiḥa overlay, the focus's spiritual-loss branch meets the petition for guidance to the straight path and the named straying in 1:6–1:7; one aspect of being in loss becomes departure from right orientation.
findings.mechanism: The focus branch describes leaving the true direction, losing good, and falling into ruin. The individual external ayat ask for guidance to the straight path and contrast it with those who stray; these separate cues return through خُسْرٍ and make loss directional.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can picture one kind of loss as going off course, with guidance as its counter-direction.
findings.containment: This overlay uses only the individual external ayat 1:6 and 1:7. They do not define all loss, prove that 103:2 lexically says straying, or authorize a whole-surah Fātiḥa reading.

epistemic.reason: The exact external path/straying cues and focus spiritual-loss branch are supplied; the relation is a bounded external overlay.
